newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit falls as dollar/majors strong in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit falls as dollar/majors strong in Asia.

text.p: The surge of the dollar against the yen in Asia pushed the ringgit lower, dealers said.
Players with bullish ringgit positions were also forced to cut their holdings ahead of the weekend, they said.
"There's dollar/ringgit short-covering. Dollar is also very strong," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
The dollar powered higher on growing epectations that the interest rate gap between Japan and the U.S. would soon widen.
Strong U.S. retail sales data boosted the dollar on Thursday as the market bet that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike rates at its open market committee meeting on March 28.
"It's interbank play today. (Dollar/ringgit) has potential to fall after this, but we'll wait for the 28th," said a corporate dealer at a large bank.
The ringgit/Sing cross traded below 0.58 Singapore dollar, trying to build up a base before attempting the resistance again, dealers said.
At 0800 GMT, ringgit was at 2.4790/95 a dollar against 2.4758/63 at its Thursday Kuala Lumpur closing.
The ringgit was also at 0.5780/90 Singapore dollar, unmoved from Thursday.
